comparison_assessments.accuracy_note: The lyric preserves the opening declaration of happiness, the singular man, and all three negative clauses in order: walking according to wicked counsel, standing on sinners' path, and sitting in mockers' seat. The walk–stand–sit progression and its distinct associations remain intact. The supplied literal rendering also closely follows the Hebrew.
comparison_assessments.creative_liberties_note: The lyric turns “in the counsel of the wicked” into “as the wicked advise.” Its habitual present “doesn't” is a defensible contextual rendering of the Hebrew perfect verbs, which the literal version represents with “has not.” The opening omits the English copula; the Hebrew likewise has no expressed copula.

comparison_assessments.accuracy_note: Preserves the opening positive assessment and the ordered threefold refusal to walk, stand, and sit among negatively characterized people. The seating image remains explicit.
comparison_assessments.creative_liberties_note: Changes third-person description to direct address. Blessedness becomes God's liking; counsel becomes habitual ruts; wickedness becomes blindness; sinners become good-for-nothings; and scoffers become know-it-alls. Standing in sinners' way is compressed to standing with them.
